back: Indirect evidence of past climate in natural archives: ice cores, tree rings, pollen, ocean sediments and fossils.
Antarctic ice cores go back about 800 000 years; bubbles show past CO2 and methane, and oxygen isotopes show temperature.
About 1.1 °C warmer in 2011-2020 than in 1850-1900 (IPCC); CO2 up from about 280 ppm to over 420 ppm; sea level up about 20 cm 1901-2018.
Heat trapped by a gas over a stated period (usually 100 years) relative to the same mass of CO2 (GWP = 1).
CO2e = mass of gas × GWP. Methane about 28, nitrous oxide about 265 (100-year values, rounded).
Solar output (about 0.1% over the sunspot cycle), volcanic aerosols (short cooling) and ENSO (year-to-year variation); none explains the long-term warming.
Fossil fuels (CO2), deforestation, livestock and rice (methane), fertilisers (N2O), F-gases and albedo change: the enhanced greenhouse effect.
El Niño: weak trades, warm water spreads east in the Pacific; southern Africa tends to be drier. La Niña: strong trades, cool eastern Pacific; southern Africa tends to be wetter.
